original_question: Given two one-variable germs tangent to the identity (multiplier 1), provide an effective and implementable decision procedure that determines whether they are holomorphically locally conjugated.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, together with its precise reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and the corresponding positive result in Theorem 1.3: an isolated-zeros principle for analytic conjugacy of one-parameter unfoldings of tangent-to-the-identity one-variable germs.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets holomorphic local conjugacy in the parabolic/tangent-to-the-identity setting and correctly centers the conjugacy problem rather than formal classification alone.
missing_details: The paper is not posed for an arbitrary pair of isolated one-variable germs; it is posed for one-parameter unfoldings, i.e. fibered germs in two variables whose fiber maps are one-variable tangent-to-the-identity germs.
The ambient class is the paper's specific class of parameter-preserving local holomorphic diffeomorphisms, not just arbitrary germs with multiplier 1.
The problem is not stated as an algorithmic or effective decision procedure.

The official formulation is an isolated-zeros/rigidity statement: fiberwise analytic conjugacies along a sequence of parameter values accumulating at 0 should force analytic conjugacy of the whole unfoldings.
One must specify the existence of a sequence of parameter values tending to 0.
One must specify that the comparison is made on the fiber restrictions of the unfoldings at those parameter values.
The paper's nearby reformulation uses additional control on the fiberwise conjugacies (the precise domain/size hypothesis introduced in Proposition 1.2), which your draft omits.
The exact notion of conjugacy is analytic conjugacy of the unfoldings as germs, not merely pairwise conjugacy of isolated one-variable germs.
The fixed-point/fiber data required in the paper's formulation are omitted.
The draft broadens the scope from the paper's narrow family-conjugacy question to the far broader general classification problem for parabolic germs.
refined_question: Let φ and η be germs of one-parameter unfoldings of tangent-to-the-identity one-variable holomorphic diffeomorphisms, in the precise fibered class considered in Section 1. Assume that, for a sequence of parameter values x_n → 0, the one-variable fiber germs φ|_{x=x_n} and η|_{x=x_n} are holomorphically conjugate under the exact auxiliary hypotheses imposed in Proposition 1.2 on those fiberwise conjugacies. Must φ and η then be analytically conjugate as germs of unfoldings?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as reformulated in Proposition 1.2, is analytic conjugacy of such unfoldings completely determined by analytic conjugacy of the corresponding one-variable fibers along an accumulating parameter sequence satisfying the paper's precise control hypothesis on the fiberwise conjugating maps?
justification: The draft is too broad and slightly mislocated. The nearest paper-faithful target is not a general effective classification problem for two isolated parabolic germs in one variable, but the introduction's isolated-zeros conjecture/reformulation/theorem about analytic conjugacy of one-parameter unfoldings. The paper's emphasis, especially in Section 1 and specifically around Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3, is whether analytic conjugacy of the whole unfolding can be detected from conjugacies of the one-variable fibers along a sequence of parameter values tending to the unperturbed one. That is the closest narrow formulation matching your draft's intuition while staying faithful to the paper.
